units: <cite ref="Niddah 16b:56">Nidd. 16ᵇ</cite> <he>הנכנס לבית חבירו פ׳</he> who enters his neighbor’s house without notice.

<cite ref="Niddah 16b:60-61">Ib.</cite> <he>ארבעה … והנכנס לביתו פ׳ וכ׳</he> four the Lord hates, and I do not love: him who enters his own house suddenly (after a long absence), not to speak of him who enters his neighbor’s house &c.; <cite ref="Vayikra Rabbah 21">Lev. R. s. 21</cite>; <cite ref="Yalkut Shimoni on Torah 382:1">Yalk. Ex. 382</cite>; Pesik. Aḥăré, p. 177ᵃ. Ib.; Lev. R. l. c. <he>אל תכנס לעיר פ׳</he> do not enter a city (in official capacity) without notice.

Num. R. s. 10 (ref. to בפתע פתאם, Num. VI, 9) בפ׳ זה שוגג … פ׳ זה אונס b’fethʿa means unintentionally, as in Num. XXXV, 22, pithom means an unavoidable accident; דבר אחר פ׳ זה מזיד וכ׳ another explanation: pithom means in heat (being carried away by passion, as פתאים (Prov. XXII, 3).
<cite ref="Bamidbar Rabbah 16:11">Num. R. s. 16</cite> <he>אני משלח להם מלאכי פ׳</he> I will send them my messenger suddenly (by surprise); a. e.
